seo.title: Homeless help in San Antonio - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help in San Antonio for people experiencing homelessness: shelter, meals, showers, health care, benefits, jobs, ID, legal help, youth, veterans, and pets.

page.heading: San Antonio homeless and housing-crisis help

content.text: Immediate danger, fire, police, or ambulance:

notice.text: Beds, schedules, routes, costs, and eligibility can change.
Call before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, treatment, benefit, money, or job the same day. Call 911 for immediate danger or a medical emergency.

content.text: If you have nowhere safe to sleep, call the City of San Antonio Community Connections Hotline at

. Ask for Homelink and say where you are, who is with you, whether anyone is pregnant or under 18, medical or mobility needs, veteran status, pets, and whether you have identification. An assessment or referral is not a promise of a bed or permanent housing.
No Home Help is an open-source directory, not an emergency service or service provider. Listings do not guarantee eligibility or availability.

items.name: Emergency services — 911

content.text: immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, trouble breathing, unconsciousness, fire, or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location and describe the danger first.
San Antonio Police Department contact guidance

items.name: Community Connections Hotline and Homelink

content.text: homeless-services navigation, shelter options, Homelink housing assessment, outreach referrals, and health or social-service connections.
Haven for Hope, 1 Haven for Hope Way, Monday–Friday, 7 a.m.–3 p.m. American GI Forum also lists limited assessment hours at 610 North Main Avenue, Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, 8:30–11:30 a.m.
Close to Home — current access points

items.name: 211 Texas

content.text: ; choose option 1 for local resources or option 2 for state benefits.
Ask for open shelter, food today, health care, benefits, rent or utility help, or a service near you. Ask the operator to confirm hours, eligibility, documents, and space before traveling.

items.name: Center for Health Care Services crisis line

content.text: For a mental-health or substance-use crisis, assessment, and direction to the right care in Bexar County. Call 911 for immediate physical danger or a medical emergency.

items.name: San Antonio 311

content.text: For city services, cooling or warming locations, outreach questions, and non-emergency local information.

items.name: Street outreach

content.text: Give a precise location, description, time last seen, mobility or health concerns, and whether there is immediate danger. Outreach is not an emergency response and cannot guarantee transport, shelter, or housing.

items.name: Haven for Hope — central homeless-services campus

content.text: 1 Haven for Hope Way, San Antonio, TX 78207
Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Services can include shelter, meals, showers, health care, documents, benefits, employment, recovery support, case management, and pet kennels.

a parent or guardian with minor children should speak with Security. A single adult may ask at the South Gate about courtyard pre-intake; this is limited, short-term safe sleeping and does not guarantee admission to a residential program.

North-campus residential eligibility and south-campus courtyard access are different. Bring any ID, medicine, and documents you have, but call if documents are missing. Ask about accessibility, bags, couples, pets, and capacity.

items.name: Homelink coordinated housing assessment

content.text: Haven for Hope, Monday–Friday, 7 a.m.–3 p.m.; American GI Forum, 610 North Main Avenue, Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, 8:30–11:30 a.m.; or another current access point.
The assessment is for possible referral to housing programs. It does not guarantee immediate shelter, a voucher, or permanent housing. Keep your phone number and usual location current.

items.name: SAMMinistries — emergency shelter and housing programs

content.text: low-barrier emergency shelter, rapid re-housing, permanent supportive housing, veteran programs, and prevention assistance. Each has separate capacity and eligibility.
. A call or assessment does not guarantee placement or financial help.

items.name: San Antonio Rescue Mission — men

content.text: 907 East Quincy Street, San Antonio, TX 78215
line up around 3:30 p.m.; check-in begins around 4 p.m., subject to capacity. The program states that a picture ID and Social Security number are requested.
Overnight shelter for men, shower, clean clothing, chapel, evening meal, and morning food. It is a Christian ministry; call first for admission, sobriety, health, bag, and ID rules.

items.name: Family Violence Prevention Services — confidential shelter

content.text: Safety planning, emergency shelter, counseling, legal help, and support for adults and children affected by domestic violence. The shelter address is confidential. Call 911 for immediate danger and use a safer device if yours may be monitored.

items.name: Opportunity Home San Antonio — public and assisted housing

content.text: Applications for public housing and other affordable properties; Housing Choice Voucher applications only when that waiting list opens. Opportunity Home warns that waits may be two to seven years.
Apply only through the official portal, save the confirmation, and keep contact and household information current. There is no fee to join a waiting list.

items.name: Corazon Day Center — weekday lunch

content.text: Monday–Friday, noon–1 p.m. The center also offers weekday case management, showers on selected days, identification help, and severe-weather services.

items.name: Christian Assistance Ministry — sack lunches and groceries

content.text: Monday–Saturday, 9–11 a.m. CAM also lists groceries, clothing, hygiene supplies, showers, prescriptions, utility help, birth-certificate help, and mail for enrolled clients.
Services can close early when daily limits are reached. Confirm which campus provides the help you need.

items.name: Church Under the Bridge — evening meals

content.text: Sunday, Tuesday, and Friday at 6 p.m.; schedule can change.
Clothing distribution is listed for the first and third Tuesday at 4 p.m. This is a Christian street ministry and not a housing program.
Church Under the Bridge — current schedule

items.name: San Antonio Food Bank — find food and benefits help

content.text: 5200 Historic Old Highway 90, San Antonio, TX 78227
Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m.; Saturday, 9 a.m.–3 p.m.
Ask for a nearby pantry or distribution, SNAP or Medicaid help, job training, senior food, or pet food. Do not assume the warehouse provides walk-in groceries at every hour; call or use the locator.
San Antonio Food Bank — get help

items.name: St. Stephen's CARE Center — client-choice pantry

content.text: 2127 South Zarzamora Street, San Antonio, TX 78207
Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–noon and 1–4 p.m. Hours, household limits, and required information may change; call first.
Catholic Charities — St. Stephen's Food Pantry

items.name: Haven for Hope meals

content.text: 1 Haven for Hope Way, San Antonio, TX 78207
Meals are part of campus and courtyard services. Access depends on enrollment or courtyard rules; ask intake or the South Gate about current access.

items.name: 211 — open food today

content.text: Give your ZIP code or nearest cross streets and ask for a meal or pantry open today, plus transport and document requirements. Call the referred provider before a long trip.

items.name: Corazon Day Center — showers and case management

content.text: Tuesday and Thursday, 9 a.m.–noon; Sunday, 8–11:30 a.m.
Other help includes weekday case management, lunch, identification recovery, hygiene items, and extended severe-weather service. Capacity can be limited.

items.name: Christian Assistance Ministry — showers, clothing, hygiene, and mail

content.text: Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday, 9:30–11:30 a.m.; Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday, 1–3 p.m.
Other help includes clothing, hygiene kits, food, limited prescriptions and utilities, ID recovery, and mail for people enrolled as homeless clients. Arrive early and confirm capacity.

items.name: Haven for Hope — basic needs and partner services

content.text: 1 Haven for Hope Way, San Antonio, TX 78207
Services can include showers, laundry, clothing, meals, mail, computers, benefits, health care, and case management for eligible campus or courtyard clients.

items.name: San Antonio Public Library — internet, charging, and Enhanced Library Card

content.text: Public computers, Wi-Fi, charging where available, information help, and library cards. The Enhanced Library Card is accepted by some local agencies as supplemental ID; it is not a state ID or proof of immigration status.

items.name: VIA Metropolitan Transit — fares and reduced fares

content.text: $1.30 standard or $0.65 reduced; transfers are free within the published limit. Confirm before travel.
Reduced fare requires an eligible VIA Reduced Fare ID. Low income alone is not listed as a qualification. Some service agencies may provide passes.

categories.title: 5. Health, dental, mental health, and recovery

items.name: CentroMed Sarah E. Davidson Clinic at Haven for Hope

content.text: 1 Haven for Hope Way, San Antonio, TX 78207
Primary care and related health services for people using the Haven campus. Call for hours, eligibility, appointments, identification, and cost.
City health and homeless resource directory

items.name: CommuniCare West Campus

content.text: Medical, dental, behavioral-health, and community health services. Ask about same-day care, sliding fees, insurance enrollment, language help, and documents.

items.name: Center for Health Care Services — mental health and substance use

content.text: 601 North Frio Street. CHCS states that people are not denied service because they cannot pay and sliding fees may apply. Call first when possible.

items.name: San Antonio Christian Dental Clinic

content.text: 1 Haven for Hope Way, Building 1, Suite 400
Free dental care for adults who meet eligibility rules. Treatment is by appointment; call for screening, documents, referral rules, and capacity.

items.name: University Health CareLink

content.text: A financial-assistance program for Bexar County residents who are uninsured and do not qualify for other coverage. CareLink is not insurance and enrollment is not automatic.

items.name: Alpha Home — substance-use treatment for women

content.text: Residential and outpatient treatment and recovery support for women. Call about assessment, funding, pregnancy or medication needs, children, and waiting time.

items.name: Lifetime Recovery — substance-use treatment

content.text: Adult residential and outpatient treatment and recovery support. Call about admission, detox needs, fees or funding, medications, ID, and beds.

items.name: San Antonio Council on Alcohol and Drug Awareness

content.text: Prevention, education, recovery support, and referral. Ask what is offered directly and where to obtain clinical assessment or treatment.

items.name: Your Texas Benefits — SNAP, Medicaid, TANF, and health programs

content.text: through the official state portal or call
Help with SNAP, Medicaid or CHIP, TANF cash help, Medicare Savings Programs, and application status. Save the application number and report contact changes.

items.name: Social Security — replacement card, SSI, and SSDI

content.text: Ask about a replacement card, SSI or SSDI, a missing payment, changing a mailing address or direct deposit, and a local-office appointment. Never pay for an appointment.

items.name: City of San Antonio Rental Assistance

content.text: The city opens its online portal for a limited period, normally the second Wednesday of the month from 1–2 p.m.; holidays can change this. Check the official page for the next opening.
Eligibility includes a current Notice to Vacate or eviction court citation and other listed documents. Funding is limited. Applying does not stop a court case; request legal help immediately.

items.name: City Utility Assistance

content.text: 1302 North Zarzamora Street, San Antonio, TX 78207

Limited CPS Energy and SAWS help for income-eligible households. Priority includes households with young children, people with disabilities, or adults age 60 and older. Call about documents and missing-document alternatives.

items.name: San Antonio Food Bank benefits assistance

content.text: Screening and application help for SNAP, Medicaid, and other programs, plus food referrals. Ask what identity, income, and household information is needed.

items.name: Workforce Solutions Alamo — South Central Career Center

content.text: Job search, computers, resumes, recruitment events, skills assessment, unemployment information, training referrals, and support-service screening. Ask what is available without ID or a permanent address.

items.name: Goodwill San Antonio Career Centers

content.text: 406 West Commerce Street, San Antonio, TX 78207
Free employment help, computers, resumes, interviews, job matching, career coaching, and training information at multiple centers. Call for current walk-in hours and documents.

items.name: Ready to Work

content.text: Training, education, coaching, and support services for eligible San Antonio residents age 18 or older who are authorized to work in the United States and meet income rules.
Screening and enrollment take time; training is not a paid job. Ask about transport, childcare, documents, high-school equivalency, and career paths.

items.name: Project QUEST

content.text: Support for eligible participants completing approved training for in-demand careers, possibly including tuition, books, supplies, testing, transport, and case management.
Support depends on eligibility and an approved plan; the program does not pay wages for time spent in training.

items.name: NXT Level Youth Opportunity Center — ages 16–24

content.text: Employment, education, career navigation, mentoring, mental-health and other support for young people disconnected from work or school. The city states that a permanent address is not required.

items.name: Christian Assistance Ministry — ID recovery and mail

content.text: Wednesday starting at 9:30 a.m., limited to the first 15 people. Arrive early and confirm.
Help obtaining identity documents and a mailing address for people enrolled as homeless clients. Ask what CAM can pay for and what evidence to bring.
Close to Home — ID recovery options

items.name: San Antonio Hope Center — ID recovery

content.text: First Presbyterian Church, 404 North Alamo Street
Monday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; Tuesday and Thursday, 9–11:30 a.m. The broader resource center is listed Monday and Wednesday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.
. Confirm location, eligibility, capacity, and papers.

items.name: SAPD HOPE Team — ID referral and outreach

content.text: Outreach and referral for people experiencing homelessness, including possible ID-recovery referral. This is not an emergency line; call 911 for immediate danger.
Close to Home — HOPE Team contact

items.name: City Right to Counsel — eviction legal help

content.text: Free legal help for eligible San Antonio residents facing eviction, through Texas RioGrande Legal Aid. Contact them as soon as you receive a notice or court papers; assistance applications do not pause an eviction case.

items.name: Texas RioGrande Legal Aid

content.text: Free civil legal help for eligible low-income people, including housing, benefits, family safety, employment, and consumer matters. Acceptance depends on issue, deadlines, conflicts, and capacity.
Texas RioGrande Legal Aid — get help

items.name: Enhanced Library Card — supplemental local identification

content.text: Bazan, Carver, Johnston, and Westfall library branches. Call
The card may help identify you to participating local organizations, but it does not replace a Texas ID, driver's license, passport, Social Security card, or immigration document.

categories.title: 9. Women, families, youth, veterans, seniors, and immigrants

items.name: Family Violence Prevention Services — domestic violence

content.text: Confidential emergency shelter, safety planning, counseling, children's services, transitional help, and legal advocacy. Call 911 for immediate danger.

items.name: Rape Crisis Center

content.text: Confidential crisis support, advocacy, counseling information, and accompaniment for survivors of sexual assault.

items.name: Youth and Young Adult Services — ages 18–24

content.text: 1919 Northwest Loop 410, Suite 100, San Antonio, TX 78213
Housing navigation and age-specific help for young adults experiencing homelessness. Ask Community Connections at
Close to Home — young adult access

items.name: Veterans — National Call Center for Homeless Veterans

content.text: Connection to VA homeless programs, outreach, health care, shelter referrals, and housing assistance for veterans and people calling on their behalf.

items.name: Endeavors — Supportive Services for Veteran Families

content.text: 3201 Cherry Ridge Drive, Building A, Suite 101
Homelessness prevention and rapid re-housing for eligible very-low-income veterans and families. Screening, funding, documents, and capacity apply.

items.name: Bexar County Military and Veterans Services Center

content.text: 1422 East Grayson Street, San Antonio, TX 78208
Benefits claims, referrals, and navigation for veterans, service members, and families. Call for appointments and discharge-document needs.

items.name: Older adults and people with disabilities

content.text: Ask about meals, transport, benefits, caregiver support, adult protective services, and help remaining safe.

items.name: The Arc of San Antonio — intellectual and developmental disabilities

content.text: Case management, family support, day services, employment and other disability resources. It is not an emergency shelter.

items.name: RAICES — immigration legal services

content.text: Immigration legal screening and representation in selected matters. A call does not create an attorney-client relationship or guarantee representation.

items.name: Caritas Legal Services — immigration help

content.text: Nonprofit immigration legal services through Catholic Charities. Ask about consultation, fees, documents, interpretation, and whether the office handles your case type.

items.name: Haven for Hope — limited kennel and cattery

content.text: 1 Haven for Hope Way, San Antonio, TX 78207
Limited kennel and cattery space for pets of enrolled clients. Call about capacity, species, vaccines, behavior, supplies, and service-animal accommodation.

items.name: DaisyCares pet food assistance

content.text: Request through Food Bank Client Services:
Pet-food assistance through participating food programs when supplies are available. Ask for the closest distribution, dates, eligibility, and stock.

items.name: San Antonio Animal Care Services

content.text: Ask about urgent animal welfare, lost pets, surrender prevention, pet-pantry events, low-cost services, and options if you may lose housing. Intake and pantry supply are not guaranteed.

items.name: Spay Neuter Network — low-cost veterinary care

content.text: 210 Tuleta Drive, Building 3, San Antonio, TX 78212
Free or low-cost spay/neuter and low-cost vaccines and wellness services. Published vaccine and wellness hours are Tuesday–Friday, 10 a.m.–2 p.m.; surgery requires an appointment.
Confirm phone, appointment, residency, income, species, and payment requirements on the official site.

items.name: Extreme heat — cooling locations and water

confusion, fainting, seizure, very hot skin, or inability to drink. Call 911, move to shade or air conditioning, loosen clothing, and cool the person.

. A fan is not safe as the only cooling method in extreme indoor heat.

content.text: . Locations and activation thresholds change with the event.
may extend hours or provide severe-weather shelter when activated; call
confusion, slurred speech, very slow breathing, or inability to wake. Call 911 and move the person somewhere dry and sheltered.
